title: Why Sleep Matters
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Most adults need seven to nine hours of sleep every night. When we sleep, our body rests and our brain sorts the things we learned during the day. Sleep is not wasted time. It helps us feel fresh and ready for tomorrow.

Many people sleep too little because they work late or look at their phones in bed. The bright light from a screen can keep the brain awake. After a few bad nights, people often feel tired, hungry and less patient.

Doctors give some simple tips. Go to bed at the same time every day. Keep your bedroom dark and quiet. Put your phone away thirty minutes before sleep. Small changes like these can make a big difference.

adult.def: a person who is fully grown
adult.g: 可數名詞，複數 adults；Most adults 表示「大多數成年人」。

rest.ex: You should rest after a long walk.
rest.g: 不及物動詞；our body rests 主詞第三人稱單數加 s。

brain.def: the part of your head that thinks and remembers
brain.ex: The brain needs a lot of energy.
brain.g: 可數名詞；the brain 指一般的大腦。

waste.def: to use something badly or not use it
waste.g: 文中 wasted time：過去分詞當形容詞，「浪費掉的時間」。

screen.def: the flat front of a phone, TV or computer
screen.g: a screen 單數；the light from a screen = 螢幕發出的光。

patient.g: less patient：less + 形容詞，表示「比較沒那麼…」。

difference.def: the way that two things are not the same
difference.g: make a difference = 產生影響、有幫助。

grammar.zh: need 後面接需要的東西。
grammar.ex: Most adults need seven to nine hours of sleep

grammar.zh: 原形動詞開頭，用來提出建議。
grammar.ex: Go to bed at the same time every day.
Keep your bedroom dark and quiet.

questions.q: How many hours of sleep do most adults need?
What can keep the brain awake?
When should you put your phone away?

keySentences.s: Sleep is not wasted time.
Small changes like these can make a big difference.

title: Busy Little Bees
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Bees are small, but they do a very big job. When a bee visits a flower, it carries pollen to the next flower. This helps plants make fruit and seeds. Many foods we eat, like apples and almonds, need bees.
A bee family lives together in a hive. One queen lays eggs, and thousands of worker bees collect food and keep the hive clean. Worker bees also make honey from the sweet juice inside flowers.
In some places, the number of bees is going down. Bees need flowers and clean places to live. People can help by growing flowers on balconies and in gardens, even in big cities.

flower.def: the colorful part of a plant

carry.def: to hold something and take it somewhere
carry.g: 第三人稱單數 carries（子音 + y → ies）。

seed.def: a small thing from which a new plant grows
seed.g: fruit and seeds：fruit 常不可數，seeds 可數。

hive.ex: The hive is full of honey.

collect.def: to bring things together from different places

honey.def: a sweet food made by bees
honey.ex: I put honey in my tea.
honey.g: 不可數名詞，不加 a 也不加 s。

juice.def: the liquid from fruit or plants
juice.g: 不可數名詞；sweet juice 甜甜的汁液。

balcony.def: a small area outside a window of a building
balcony.ex: We have plants on our balcony.
balcony.g: 複數 balconies；on balconies 在陽台上。

grammar.zh: When + 句子，表示「當…的時候」。
grammar.ex: When a bee visits a flower, it carries pollen to the next flower.

grammar.pt: 現在進行式表示變化中
grammar.zh: is going down 表示數量正在減少。
grammar.ex: the number of bees is going down
People can help by growing flowers

questions.q: What do bees carry from flower to flower?
Who lays eggs in the hive?
How can people in cities help bees?

keySentences.s: A bee family lives together in a hive.
This helps plants make fruit and seeds.

title: Giving Plastic a Second Life
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Every year, people around the world use millions of tons of plastic. Bottles, bags and boxes are useful, but many of them are used only once. After that, they often end up in the ground or in the sea.
Recycling can give plastic a second life. Old bottles can become new bottles, clothes or even park benches. But recycling only works well when people clean their plastic and put it in the right bin.
Using less plastic is even better. You can carry a water bottle, bring your own shopping bag and say no to straws. If many people make these small changes, there will be less waste.

plastic.def: a light material made in factories
plastic.ex: This chair is made of plastic.
plastic.g: 不可數名詞；也可當形容詞 a plastic bag。

useful.ex: A map is useful when you travel.

recycle.def: to make used things into new things
recycle.g: 動名詞 recycling 可當主詞：Recycling can give…

bench.def: a long seat for two or more people
bench.ex: We sat on a bench in the park.
bench.g: 複數 benches（-ch 結尾加 es）。

bin.ex: Put it in the recycling bin.
bin.g: in the right bin 放進正確的桶子。

straw.g: say no to straws：say no to + 名詞 = 拒絕。

waste.g: 不可數名詞，用 less 修飾。

grammar.ex: they often end up in the ground or in the sea
recycling only works well when people clean their plastic

grammar.zh: If + 現在式，主句用 will。
grammar.ex: If many people make these small changes, there will be less waste.

questions.q: What often happens to plastic after one use?
opts: It ends up in the ground or sea

questions.q: When does recycling work well?
opts: When people clean it and use the right bin

questions.q: What is even better than recycling?

keySentences.s: Using less plastic is even better.
Recycling can give plastic a second life.

title: Try something new for 30 days

source.name: TED：Matt Cutts, Try something new for 30 days

note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: Is there something you always wanted to do but never started? In a short and light TED talk, Matt Cutts gives a simple idea: try it for just thirty days.
Thirty days is not very long, so the goal does not feel too hard. You can try to walk every day, read a page of a book, or take one photo each day. If you miss a day, you can start again.
Small daily goals can build new habits. After a month, you may feel more confident and want to try another challenge. What would you like to try for the next thirty days?

goal.def: something you want to do in the future
goal.ex: My goal is to run five kilometers.
goal.g: 可數名詞；daily goals 每天的目標。

simple.g: a simple idea：simple 以子音開頭用 a。

miss.def: to not do or have something you planned
miss.g: If you miss a day 如果漏掉一天。

daily.ex: Exercise is part of my daily life.

habit.def: something you do often, usually without thinking
habit.g: build a habit 養成習慣。

confident.def: sure that you can do something well
confident.ex: She feels confident in English class.

challenge.def: something new and difficult to do
challenge.ex: Learning to swim was a challenge.

month.g: After a month 一個月後。

grammar.ex: You can try to walk every day
Thirty days is not very long
What would you like to try for the next thirty days?

questions.q: How long does the talk suggest you try something new?
What can you do if you miss a day?
What can small daily goals build?

keySentences.s: If you miss a day, you can start again.
Small daily goals can build new habits.

title: Drink More Water
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: About sixty percent of the human body is water. We lose water every day when we breathe, sweat and go to the toilet. That is why we need to drink water again and again.
When we do not drink enough, we may get a headache or feel tired. In hot weather or after sports, the body needs even more water. Many people forget to drink because they are busy.
Here are some easy ideas. Keep a bottle on your desk. Drink a glass of water with every meal. Eat fruit like watermelon and oranges. Your body will thank you.

percent.g: 數字 + percent，percent 不加 s。

lose.g: 過去式 lost；We lose water 我們流失水分。

breathe.def: to take air into your body and let it out

sweat.def: to make water come out of your skin
sweat.ex: I sweat a lot in summer.
sweat.g: 過去式 sweated 或 sweat。

forget.g: forget to + 動詞 = 忘記去做。

meal.def: food eaten at one time, like lunch
meal.ex: We have three meals a day.
meal.g: with every meal 每餐都…；every 後接單數。

grammar.ex: That is why we need to drink water again and again.
the body needs even more water
Many people forget to drink because they are busy.

questions.q: How much of the human body is water?
What may happen if you don't drink enough?
Which is one easy idea from the article?
opts: Keep a bottle on your desk

keySentences.s: Drink a glass of water with every meal.
About sixty percent of the human body is water.

title: Cities on Two Wheels
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: In many cities, more people are riding bicycles to school and work. Bikes are cheap, quiet and good for the air. Riding a bike is also good exercise, so it helps people stay healthy.
Some cities build special bike lanes to keep riders safe from cars. Many places also have public bikes. You can rent a bike with a card or a phone app and return it at another station.
Of course, riders must follow the rules. Wear a helmet, use lights at night and stop at red lights. With care, a bike can be a fast and fun way to get around.

ride.def: to sit on a bike or horse and control it
ride.ex: I ride my bike to school.
ride.g: 過去式 rode；riding 是 -ing 形。

lane.def: a part of a road for one line of traffic

safe.g: keep + 人 + safe from + 危險。

rent.def: to pay to use something for a short time
rent.g: rent a bike 租一台腳踏車。

helmet.def: a hard hat that protects your head
helmet.g: wear a helmet 戴安全帽。

rule.def: something that tells you what you must do
rule.g: follow the rules 遵守規則。

grammar.zh: more people are riding 表示越來越多人在騎。
grammar.ex: more people are riding bicycles to school and work
riders must follow the rules
a fast and fun way to get around

questions.q: Why are bikes good for the air?
How can you rent a public bike?
opts: With a card or phone app

questions.q: What should riders wear?

keySentences.s: Of course, riders must follow the rules.
Bikes are cheap, quiet and good for the air.

title: A Night at the Market
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Night markets are a big part of life in Taiwan. When the sun goes down, streets fill with food stands, games and bright lights. Families, students and tourists walk slowly and look for something tasty.
Popular snacks include bubble tea, fried chicken and stinky tofu. Many stands sell small dishes, so people can try many different foods in one night. Prices are usually low.
Night markets can be crowded and noisy, but that is part of the fun. If you visit, bring some cash, a small bag for trash and an empty stomach!

market.def: a place where people buy and sell things
market.ex: We buy fruit at the market.

stand.def: a small table or shop outside where things are sold

tourist.def: a person who travels for fun

tasty.g: something tasty：形容詞放在 something 後面。

snack.def: a small amount of food between meals
snack.ex: I eat a snack at 3 p.m.

fried.g: fry 的過去分詞當形容詞。

crowded.g: crowd 人群 → crowded 擁擠的。

grammar.ex: When the sun goes down, streets fill with food stands
Many stands sell small dishes, so people can try many different foods

grammar.zh: something 的形容詞要放後面。
grammar.ex: look for something tasty

questions.q: When do night markets start?
Why can people try many foods in one night?
What should you bring?

keySentences.s: Night markets are a big part of life in Taiwan.
Popular snacks include bubble tea, fried chicken and stinky tofu.

title: How to spot fake AI photos
zh: 如何看穿 AI 假照片

source.name: TED：Hany Farid, How to spot fake AI photos

note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: Computers can now make pictures that look very real. In this TED talk, Hany Farid, an expert in digital photos, talks about how fake pictures can fool people online.

He helps journalists and courts check if a picture is real. He also shares tips that anyone can use. For example, real photos follow the rules of light, shadow and distance, and fake ones often make mistakes.
The most important tip is simple: slow down. Before you believe or share a shocking picture, stop for a moment and check where it came from.

expert.def: a person who knows a lot about something
expert.ex: She is an expert in computers.

shadow.def: a dark shape made when light is blocked
shadow.ex: My shadow is long in the evening.

believe.def: to think that something is true

shocking.def: very surprising in a bad way

grammar.ex: pictures that look very real
check if a picture is real
Before you believe or share a shocking picture, stop for a moment

questions.q: What is Hany Farid an expert in?
What do real photos follow?
opts: The rules of light and shadow

questions.q: What is the most important tip?

keySentences.s: He helps journalists and courts check if a picture is real.
Before you believe or share a shocking picture, stop for a moment and check where it came from.

title: Our Friend the Moon
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: The Moon is about 384,000 kilometers away from Earth. It does not make its own light. We can see it because it reflects light from the Sun. Its shape seems to change during the month.
The Moon also pulls on the sea. This pull helps make the tides go up and down along the beach. Without the Moon, our oceans would be very different.
In 1969, astronauts walked on the Moon for the first time. Today, several countries plan new trips there. Maybe one day, people will live and work on the Moon.

kilometer.ex: It is five kilometers to school.

reflect.def: to send back light or heat
reflect.g: reflects light from the Sun 反射太陽光。

shape.ex: The cake has a heart shape.

seem.g: seem to + 原形：seems to change。

pull.ex: Pull the door to open it.
pull.g: 文中 This pull 當名詞。

tide.def: the rise and fall of the sea

astronaut.def: a person who travels into space
astronaut.ex: She wants to be an astronaut.

several.def: more than two but not many
several.ex: I have several friends in Japan.

grammar.ex: It does not make its own light.

grammar.zh: Without… 搭配 would 表示假設。
grammar.ex: Without the Moon, our oceans would be very different.
astronauts walked on the Moon for the first time

questions.q: Why can we see the Moon?
What does the Moon help make?
When did people first walk on the Moon?

keySentences.s: The Moon also pulls on the sea.
Its shape seems to change during the month.

title: The Story of Coffee
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Coffee comes from the seeds of a small red fruit. People call these seeds coffee beans. After farmers pick the fruit, the beans are dried, roasted and then ground into powder.
Today, coffee is one of the most popular drinks in the world. Some people drink it black, and others add milk or sugar. Many offices and schools have coffee machines.
Coffee has caffeine, which helps people feel awake. But too much caffeine can make it hard to sleep. Most doctors say that a few cups a day are fine for healthy adults.

bean.def: a seed of some plants that you can eat or use

farmer.def: a person who works on a farm

powder.def: very small pieces of a dry thing

popular.g: one of the most popular + 複數名詞。

healthy.def: not sick; good for your body
healthy.g: health 名詞 → healthy 形容詞。

grammar.pt: 被動式 are + 過去分詞
grammar.ex: the beans are dried, roasted and then ground into powder

grammar.pt: one of the most + 形容詞 + 複數名詞
grammar.ex: coffee is one of the most popular drinks in the world

grammar.zh: which 引導子句補充前面的名詞。
grammar.ex: Coffee has caffeine, which helps people feel awake.

questions.q: What are coffee beans?
What can too much caffeine do?
What do most doctors say?
opts: A few cups a day are fine

keySentences.s: People call these seeds coffee beans.
Coffee has caffeine, which helps people feel awake.

title: The Power of a Walk
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Walking is one of the easiest kinds of exercise. You do not need special clothes or a gym. You only need comfortable shoes and a little time.
Studies show that a thirty-minute walk each day is good for the heart. Walking can also help people think more clearly and feel less stressed. Many people get their best ideas during a walk.
You can add walking to your day in simple ways. Get off the bus one stop early. Take the stairs instead of the elevator. Walk and talk with a friend after dinner.

gym.def: a room or building for exercise
gym.ex: I go to the gym on Mondays.

heart.ex: Exercise is good for the heart.
heart.g: be good for + 名詞 = 對…有益。

clearly.def: in a way that is easy to understand

stressed.g: feel less stressed 壓力比較小。

stairs.def: steps that go from one floor to another

grammar.ex: You do not need special clothes or a gym.
Take the stairs instead of the elevator.
Studies show that a thirty-minute walk each day is good for the heart.

questions.q: What do you need for walking?
How long is a good daily walk?
Which is one way to walk more?

keySentences.s: Take the stairs instead of the elevator.
You do not need special clothes or a gym.

title: How to speak so that people want to listen

source.name: TED：Julian Treasure, How to speak so that people want to listen

note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: Have you ever felt that people are not listening to you? In this popular TED talk, sound expert Julian Treasure talks about how to speak so that people want to listen.
He explains some habits that make listeners stop paying attention, such as complaining all the time. He also talks about the voice as a tool, like an instrument we all play.
We can change how we sound. We can speak a little slower, change our pitch and use short pauses. He even shows some warm-up exercises for the voice before an important talk.

listen.def: to pay attention to sounds or words

attention.def: the act of watching or listening carefully

complain.def: to say that you are not happy about something

voice.def: the sound you make when you speak

instrument.def: an object used to make music
instrument.ex: The piano is my favorite instrument.

pause.ex: Take a pause before you answer.

grammar.pt: Have you ever + 過去分詞
grammar.ex: Have you ever felt that people are not listening to you?
how to speak so that people want to listen
We can speak a little slower

questions.q: What is Julian Treasure an expert in?
Which habit makes people stop listening?
What does he compare the voice to?

keySentences.s: We can change how we sound.
Have you ever felt that people are not listening to you?

title: The Lungs of the Earth
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Rainforests are thick forests where it rains almost every day. They cover only a small part of the Earth, but more than half of all kinds of plants and animals live there.
Rainforest trees take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen. Because of this, people sometimes call rainforests the lungs of the Earth. Many medicines also come from rainforest plants.
Sadly, people cut down large areas of rainforest every year for farms and wood. When the trees are gone, animals lose their homes. Protecting these forests helps everyone on the planet.

forest.def: a large area covered with trees

cover.def: to be over the top of something
cover.g: cover only a small part 只覆蓋一小部分。

animal.def: a living thing that is not a plant or person
animal.g: plants and animals 植物和動物。

oxygen.def: a gas that we need to breathe

medicine.def: something you take to get better
medicine.g: Many medicines 許多藥物（種類可數）。

wood.ex: The table is made of wood.

protect.def: to keep someone or something safe
protect.ex: Protect your eyes from the sun.
protect.g: Protecting 動名詞當主詞，後面動詞用單數 helps。

grammar.ex: more than half of all kinds of plants and animals live there
Because of this, people sometimes call rainforests the lungs of the Earth.

grammar.pt: When 子句 + 被動含意
grammar.zh: When the trees are gone 當樹木消失時。
grammar.ex: When the trees are gone, animals lose their homes.

questions.q: How often does it rain in rainforests?
Why are rainforests called the lungs of the Earth?
Why do people cut down rainforests?

keySentences.s: Many medicines also come from rainforest plants.
When the trees are gone, animals lose their homes.

title: Learning a New Language
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Learning a new language takes time, and everyone makes mistakes. That is normal. Children often learn by listening and copying, and adults can learn in the same way.
Many teachers say it is better to study a little every day than a lot once a week. Fifteen minutes of reading, listening or speaking each day can help your brain remember new words.
Try to use the language in real life. Watch videos you enjoy, change your phone to English or talk with a friend. When learning is fun, it is easier to keep going.

language.def: a system of words used by people
language.g: a new language 一種新語言。

normal.ex: It is normal to feel nervous.
normal.g: That is normal. 那很正常。

copy.def: to do the same thing as someone else

remember.def: to keep something in your mind
remember.g: help + 受詞 + 原形動詞：help your brain remember。

fun.g: learning is fun 學習很有趣。

grammar.ex: Learning a new language takes time

grammar.zh: 做 A 比做 B 好。
grammar.ex: it is better to study a little every day than a lot once a week
When learning is fun, it is easier to keep going.

questions.q: What does everyone do when learning a language?
What do many teachers say is better?
Which is a way to use English in real life?

keySentences.s: Try to use the language in real life.
When learning is fun, it is easier to keep going.

title: When a Typhoon Comes
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: A typhoon is a very strong storm that starts over warm sea water. It brings heavy rain and strong winds. In Taiwan, typhoons usually come in summer and early autumn.
Weather experts watch typhoons closely and warn people early. When a big typhoon is coming, schools and offices may close, and some flights are canceled.
Before a typhoon, people buy food and water, charge their phones and bring things inside from their balconies. During the storm, it is safest to stay at home and away from windows.

storm.def: very bad weather with strong wind and rain

heavy.def: large in amount; weighing a lot
heavy.g: heavy rain 大雨（不說 big rain）。

usually.g: 頻率副詞放在一般動詞前。

warn.def: to tell someone about a danger
warn.ex: They warned us about the storm.
warn.g: warn people early 提早警告民眾。

flight.g: some flights are canceled 被動式。

charge.def: to put electricity into a battery

grammar.pt: 現在進行式表示即將發生
grammar.zh: is coming 表示快要來了。
grammar.ex: When a big typhoon is coming, schools and offices may close

grammar.zh: be + 過去分詞，表示被取消。
grammar.ex: some flights are canceled
it is safest to stay at home

questions.q: Where does a typhoon start?
What may close when a big typhoon comes?
What is safest during the storm?
opts: Stay at home away from windows

keySentences.s: It brings heavy rain and strong winds.
In Taiwan, typhoons usually come in summer and early autumn.

title: Inside the mind of a master procrastinator
zh: 拖延大師的腦袋裡在想什麼

source.name: TED：Tim Urban, Inside the mind of a master procrastinator

note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: Do you often wait until the last minute to finish your work? Writer Tim Urban says he has this habit too. His TED talk about putting things off is one of the funniest and most popular talks.
He describes the mind of a procrastinator with funny drawings. When a deadline gets close, a sudden feeling of panic finally makes him start working.
But some things in life have no deadline, like our health, our families and our dreams. He asks us to think about what we are putting off before it is too late.

finish.def: to do the last part of something
finish.g: to finish your work 不定詞。

writer.def: a person who writes books or articles

describe.def: to say what something is like
describe.g: describes the mind 描述大腦。

deadline.def: the time by which something must be done

sudden.g: a sudden feeling 一股突然的感覺。

dream.def: something you really want to do

paras: Tea is one of the oldest drinks in the world. It is made by pouring hot water over dried tea leaves. Green tea, black tea and oolong tea all come from the same plant.
Taiwan is famous for its oolong tea, which grows on cool, high mountains. Bubble tea, another drink from Taiwan, is now popular in many countries.
Tea is also part of how people meet and relax. In many homes, people offer tea to guests. Sharing a cup of tea is a simple way to say welcome.

title: Electric Cars on the Road
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: More and more people are driving electric cars. These cars do not use gas. Instead, they use a big battery that people charge at home or at charging stations.
Electric cars are quiet and do not make smoke, so they can help keep city air cleaner. They also cost less to drive, because electricity is usually cheaper than gas.
However, electric cars can be expensive to buy, and drivers sometimes worry about finding a place to charge. As batteries get better, these problems may become smaller.

title: Helping Others by Volunteering
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: A volunteer is a person who helps others without getting paid. Volunteers clean beaches, read to children, help old people and work at events.

Volunteering is good for the community, but it is also good for the volunteers. Many people say that helping others makes them feel happier and less lonely. They also meet new friends and learn new skills.
You do not need much time to start. Many groups need help for just a few hours a month. Think about what you enjoy, and find a group that needs those skills.

title: Do schools kill creativity?

source.name: TED：Sir Ken Robinson, Do schools kill creativity?

note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: This talk by Sir Ken Robinson is one of the most watched TED talks of all time. He was an education expert, and he spoke with a lot of humor.
His big idea is that creativity is as important in school as reading and math. He makes a case for an education system that helps children's creativity grow instead of stopping it.
Children are not afraid to try new things or to be wrong. As people grow up, many lose this. The talk asks parents and teachers to think about how we can keep that creative spirit alive.

title: Power from the Sun
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Every hour, the Sun sends more energy to Earth than people use in a whole year. Solar panels catch some of this sunlight and turn it into electricity.
You can see solar panels on roofs, farms and even on top of parking lots. Solar power does not make smoke, so it is good for the air and the climate.
The sun does not shine at night, so people store extra electricity in big batteries. As solar panels get cheaper, more homes and businesses are using them.

title: A Dog's Life
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Dogs have lived with people for thousands of years. They were probably the first animals that humans kept. Today, there are hundreds of kinds of dogs, from tiny to very large.
Dogs are smart and loyal. They can learn many words and understand our feelings. Some dogs work as guide dogs for blind people, and others help police or find people after earthquakes.
Having a dog is fun, but it is also a big job. Dogs need food, walks, training and visits to the vet. A good owner takes care of a dog for its whole life.

title: Robots at Work
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: A robot is a machine that can do jobs by itself. In factories, robots build cars and phones. They work fast, do not get tired and can lift heavy things.
Robots are now moving into new places. Some clean floors at home, some carry food in restaurants and some help doctors in hospitals. A few robots can even talk with people.
Some workers worry that robots will take their jobs. Others think robots will do boring or dangerous work, so people can do more creative jobs. Either way, learning new skills is important.

title: How great leaders inspire action
zh: 偉大的領導者如何激勵行動

source.name: TED：Simon Sinek, How great leaders inspire action

note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: Simon Sinek's TED talk is about leadership and why some people and companies inspire us more than others. It is one of the most viewed TED talks.
He draws a simple picture called the golden circle. In the middle is the question "Why?" Around it are "How?" and "What?" He says inspiring leaders start with why.
His examples include Apple, Martin Luther King Jr. and the Wright brothers. The idea is useful for anyone: when you explain why you do something, people understand you better.

company.ex: He works for a big company.

title: When the Ground Shakes
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: The outside of the Earth is made of huge pieces of rock that move very slowly. When two pieces suddenly slip, the ground shakes. This is an earthquake.
Taiwan has many earthquakes because it sits where these pieces meet. Most of them are small, and people hardly feel them. Strong ones can damage roads and buildings.
It is smart to be ready. Keep water, a flashlight and a first aid kit at home. When the ground shakes, drop to the floor, cover your head and hold on to something strong.

title: Why Libraries Still Matter

paras: A library is more than a room full of books. Today, libraries lend e-books, movies and even tools. Many also have free Wi-Fi, computers and quiet places to study.
Libraries are open to everyone, rich or poor, young or old. Children join story time, students prepare for exams and older people take computer classes.
With a library card, you can borrow books for free. If you are learning English, ask for easy readers or audiobooks. It is a cheap and friendly way to keep learning.

title: Shopping with One Click
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Online shopping lets us buy almost anything without leaving home. With one click, a new shirt, a book or even dinner can arrive at the door, sometimes on the same day.
It is fast and easy, and it is easy to compare prices. But it also creates a lot of boxes and plastic. Some people buy things they do not really need.
Before you click "buy," ask yourself a few questions. Do I really need it? Can I get it from a store nearby? Thinking first can save money and reduce waste.

title: The power of vulnerability

source.name: TED：Brené Brown, The power of vulnerability

note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: Brené Brown is a researcher who studies human connection: our ability to understand others, to belong and to love. Her TED talk is one of the most watched in the world.
The main idea is about vulnerability. This means being open and honest about our feelings, even when it feels risky. Many people try to hide their weak points to look strong.
But real connection needs openness. When we let others see who we really are, we can build deeper friendships. Saying "I need help" or "I'm not sure" can take courage.

title: Trees Make Cities Better
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Trees are not only beautiful. In a city, they give shade on hot days and can make streets several degrees cooler. They also clean the air and give homes to birds.
Studies show that people who live near trees often feel calmer and walk more. Trees can also help stop flooding, because their roots take in rainwater.
Many cities now plan to plant more trees along streets and in schools. Even one tree near your home can make a difference to the air and to your mood.

title: Music and Your Brain

paras: Have you ever heard an old song and suddenly remembered a place or a person? Music is closely connected to memory and feelings in our brain.
Scientists have found that music can change our mood. Fast songs can give us energy, and slow songs can help us relax. Some hospitals even use music to help patients feel less pain.
Music can also help you learn English. Singing along helps you remember words and practice pronunciation. Choose songs with clear words, read the lyrics and sing!

Trains are comfortable and on time, and they make less pollution than cars or planes. Passengers can read, work or sleep during the trip.

title: Your body language may shape who you are

She talks about "power posing," which means standing in a confident way, with your back straight and arms open, even when you do not feel confident.

Astronauts from different countries live and work there for months. They do experiments to learn how plants, animals and the human body change in space.

title: The Cost of Cheap Clothes

paras: Fast fashion means clothes that are made quickly and sold cheaply. Stores change their styles very often, so people buy new clothes all the time.
But cheap clothes have hidden costs. Making them uses a lot of water and energy. People often wear new clothes only a few times and then throw them away.
You can help by buying fewer but better clothes, taking care of them and trading with friends. Second-hand shops are also a fun place to find something special.

throw.g: throw them away 把它們丟掉：代名詞放 throw 和 away 中間。

trade.def: to give something and get something back
trade.g: trading with friends 和朋友交換。

grammar.ex: clothes that are made quickly and sold cheaply

grammar.zh: 數量少但品質好（fewer 修飾可數名詞）。
grammar.ex: buying fewer but better clothes
You can help by buying fewer but better clothes

questions.q: What does fast fashion mean?
opts: Clothes made quickly and sold cheaply

questions.q: What is one hidden cost?
opts: Using a lot of water and energy

questions.q: How can you help?

keySentences.s: But cheap clothes have hidden costs.
Fast fashion means clothes that are made quickly and sold cheaply.

title: What makes a good life? Lessons from the longest study on happiness

source.name: TED：Robert Waldinger, What makes a good life? Lessons from the longest study on happiness

note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: What keeps us happy and healthy as we go through life? Many young people think the answer is fame or money. In this TED talk, psychiatrist Robert Waldinger shares a very long study about this question.
The study followed the same group of people for many decades. The researchers checked their health, their jobs and their families again and again.
The main lesson is about good relationships. People who stay close to family, friends and community tend to be happier and healthier. So call a friend today. It may be good for you.

money.def: coins and paper used to buy things

lesson.g: The main lesson 主要的教訓。

relationship.g: good relationships 良好的人際關係。

grammar.ex: What keeps us happy and healthy as we go through life?
The study followed the same group of people for many decades.
tend to be happier and healthier

questions.q: What do many young people think brings happiness?
How long did the study follow people?
What is the main lesson?

keySentences.s: The main lesson is about good relationships.
Many young people think the answer is fame or money.

title: Laughter Is Good for You
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Everyone laughs, in every language and culture. Babies start to laugh when they are only a few months old. Laughter helps people feel close to each other.
When we laugh, we breathe more deeply and our muscles relax. Many people say they feel less stressed after a good laugh with friends.
Laughter is also contagious. When one person starts laughing, others often join in. So watch a funny video, tell a joke or spend time with people who make you smile.

laugh.def: to make sounds because something is funny

culture.def: the way of life of a group of people

contagious.def: easily spread from one person to another
contagious.g: contagious 也可以指疾病會傳染。

join.def: to become part of a group or activity

smile.g: make + 人 + 原形：make you smile。

grammar.ex: Babies start to laugh when they are only a few months old.
Laughter helps people feel close to each other.
spend time with people who make you smile

questions.q: When do babies start to laugh?
How do people feel after laughing?
What does contagious mean here?

keySentences.s: Everyone laughs, in every language and culture.
Laughter helps people feel close to each other.

title: More Than Just Games
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Video games are one of the most popular kinds of fun in the world. People play them on phones, computers and game consoles, alone or with friends online.
Some games can help players think quickly, solve problems and work as a team. Many players also learn English words from game stories and chats.
But too much gaming can hurt sleep, eyes and schoolwork. Experts suggest taking breaks and setting a time limit. Games are best when they are one part of a balanced life.

game.def: an activity you play for fun

console.def: a machine for playing video games

team.def: a group that works or plays together
team.g: work as a team 團隊合作。

balanced.def: with the right amount of each part
balanced.g: a balanced life 平衡的生活。

grammar.ex: alone or with friends online
Experts suggest taking breaks and setting a time limit.
Games are best when they are one part of a balanced life.

questions.q: Where do people play video games?
What can some games help players do?
What do experts suggest?
opts: Take breaks and set a time limit

keySentences.s: Experts suggest taking breaks and setting a time limit.
But too much gaming can hurt sleep, eyes and schoolwork.

title: Taiwan's Highest Mountain
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Yushan, or Jade Mountain, is the highest mountain in Taiwan. It is 3,952 meters tall, which makes it one of the highest peaks in East Asia.
Every year, many hikers try to climb to the top. Most of them start very early in the morning so they can watch the sunrise above the clouds.
Climbing Yushan needs planning. Hikers must apply for a permit, bring warm clothes and check the weather. Near the top, the air is thin and cold, so walking slowly is a good idea.

hiker.def: a person who walks in the mountains

sunrise.def: the time when the sun comes up

cloud.def: a white or gray mass in the sky
cloud.g: above the clouds 在雲之上。

permit.def: an official paper that lets you do something
permit.g: apply for a permit 申請許可。

grammar.ex: It is 3,952 meters tall, which makes it one of the highest peaks in East Asia.
start very early in the morning so they can watch the sunrise

grammar.zh: V-ing 當主詞，動詞用單數。
grammar.ex: Climbing Yushan needs planning.

questions.q: How tall is Yushan?
Why do hikers start early?
What must hikers apply for?

keySentences.s: Every year, many hikers try to climb to the top.
Yushan, or Jade Mountain, is the highest mountain in Taiwan.

title: Grit: The power of passion and perseverance
zh: 恆毅力：熱情與堅持的力量

source.name: TED：Angela Lee Duckworth, Grit: The power of passion and perseverance

note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: Angela Lee Duckworth left a high-paying job to teach math to seventh graders in a New York public school. There, she noticed something important.
She saw that IQ was not the only thing that separated successful students from students who struggled. In her talk, she explains her idea of "grit" as a predictor of success.
Grit means passion and perseverance for long-term goals. It is like running a marathon, not a short race. The good news is that we can keep working on it.

public.def: for everyone; run by the government

notice.def: to see or become aware of something

struggle.g: students who struggled 學得吃力的學生。

passion.def: a strong feeling of liking something
passion.ex: She has a passion for music.

perseverance.def: continuing to try even when it is hard

marathon.def: a long running race of about 42 km
marathon.g: like running a marathon 像跑馬拉松。

grammar.ex: the only thing that separated successful students from students who struggled
It is like running a marathon, not a short race.
The good news is that we can keep working on it.

questions.q: What did Duckworth teach?
What is grit?
What is grit compared to?

keySentences.s: There, she noticed something important.
It is like running a marathon, not a short race.

title: How Habits Work
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: A habit is something we do again and again, often without thinking. Brushing your teeth, checking your phone and drinking coffee in the morning are all habits.
Many habits start with a cue, like a time or a place. Then comes the action, and then a reward, like a good feeling. When this happens many times, the brain makes it automatic.
To build a good habit, start very small. Put your running shoes by the door, or read one page before bed. Small steps, repeated every day, can lead to big changes.

brush.ex: Brush your teeth twice a day.

teeth.def: the hard white things in your mouth

cue.ex: The bell is a cue to stop.

reward.def: something good you get for doing something

automatic.g: makes it automatic 讓它變成自動。

repeat.g: repeated every day 每天重複的（過去分詞）。

grammar.zh: 多個 V-ing 當主詞，動詞用複數 are。
grammar.ex: Brushing your teeth, checking your phone and drinking coffee in the morning are all habits.

grammar.zh: 倒裝：Then + 動詞 + 主詞。
grammar.ex: Then comes the action
To build a good habit, start very small.

questions.q: What is a habit?
opts: Something we do again and again

questions.q: What usually comes after the action?
How should you build a good habit?

keySentences.s: Many habits start with a cue, like a time or a place.
Small steps, repeated every day, can lead to big changes.

title: How Do We Know Tomorrow's Weather?
zh: 我們怎麼知道明天的天氣？
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Weather forecasts tell us if we need an umbrella or a jacket. But how do forecasters know what will happen tomorrow?
They collect information from weather stations, balloons, ships and satellites in space. Then powerful computers use this data to predict how the air will move.
Forecasts for the next day are usually quite correct, but forecasts for next week are harder. The weather can change quickly, so it is a good idea to check again before you go out.

forecast.def: a statement about what will happen

umbrella.def: a thing that keeps rain off you

satellite.def: a machine that goes around the Earth in space

grammar.zh: tell us if… 告訴我們是否…。
grammar.ex: Weather forecasts tell us if we need an umbrella or a jacket.

grammar.zh: predict how the air will move 預測空氣會怎麼移動。
grammar.ex: predict how the air will move
forecasts for next week are harder

questions.q: Where does weather information come from?
What do powerful computers do?
opts: Predict how the air will move

questions.q: Which forecasts are harder?

keySentences.s: But how do forecasters know what will happen tomorrow?
Weather forecasts tell us if we need an umbrella or a jacket.

title: The Sweet Story of Chocolate
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Chocolate comes from cacao beans, which grow in pods on cacao trees in hot, wet places. The beans are dried, roasted and ground to make chocolate.
Long ago in Central America, people made a bitter chocolate drink. Much later, sugar and milk were added, and chocolate became the sweet treat many people love today.
Dark chocolate has more cacao and less sugar than milk chocolate. A small piece can be a nice treat, but eating too much chocolate is not good for your teeth or your health.

chocolate.def: a sweet brown food made from cacao
chocolate.g: 通常不可數：a piece of chocolate。

pod.def: a long case that holds seeds
pod.g: grow in pods 長在豆莢裡。

wet.g: hot, wet places 炎熱潮濕的地方。

ground.zh: 被磨碎的（grind 的過去分詞）
ground.ex: The coffee beans are ground every morning.

bitter.def: having a strong, not sweet taste
bitter.g: a bitter drink 苦的飲料。

grammar.ex: Chocolate comes from cacao beans, which grow in pods on cacao trees
sugar and milk were added

grammar.pt: more A and less B than
grammar.zh: 比…有更多 A、較少 B。
grammar.ex: Dark chocolate has more cacao and less sugar than milk chocolate.

questions.q: Where do cacao beans grow?
What was the first chocolate drink like?
What does dark chocolate have more of?

keySentences.s: The beans are dried, roasted and ground to make chocolate.
Dark chocolate has more cacao and less sugar than milk chocolate.

title: How to make stress your friend

source.name: TED：Kelly McGonigal, How to make stress your friend

note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: Stress makes your heart beat fast, your breathing quicken and your forehead sweat. Many people think stress is always bad for our health.

In this TED talk, health psychologist Kelly McGonigal shares research that suggests stress may be worse for you when you believe it is harmful. How we think about stress can change how our body reacts.
She also talks about an often forgotten way to handle stress: reaching out to other people. Asking for help, or helping someone else, can make us stronger in hard times.

stress.def: a feeling of worry because of problems
stress.ex: I am under a lot of stress.

beat.def: to make a regular sound or movement
beat.g: make + 受詞 + 原形：makes your heart beat。

forehead.def: the part of your face above your eyes

react.g: how our body reacts 身體如何反應。

reach.def: to stretch out your hand; to contact
reach.g: reach out to + 人 = 向…求助、聯絡。

grammar.ex: Stress makes your heart beat fast
stress may be worse for you when you believe it is harmful
Asking for help, or helping someone else, can make us stronger in hard times.

questions.q: What does stress make your heart do?
When may stress be worse for you?
opts: When you believe it is harmful

questions.q: What is an often forgotten way to handle stress?

keySentences.s: Many people think stress is always bad for our health.
How we think about stress can change how our body reacts.

title: Every Drop Counts
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Water covers most of the Earth, but only a very small part of it is fresh water that people can drink. In dry seasons, some places do not have enough.
Saving water at home is easy. Turn off the tap while you brush your teeth. Take shorter showers. Fix leaks quickly, because a dripping tap can waste a lot of water in a year.
You can also reuse water. Water from washing vegetables can water your plants. Every drop counts. If everyone saves a little, together we can save a lot.

drop.def: a very small amount of liquid
drop.g: Every drop counts 每一滴都算數。

season.def: one of the parts of the year

tap.def: a thing that controls water from a pipe

shower.def: washing your body under running water
shower.ex: I take a shower every night.

leak.def: a hole where water comes out
leak.ex: There is a leak in the roof.

drip.g: a dripping tap 滴水的水龍頭。

grammar.pt: only a very small part of
grammar.ex: only a very small part of it is fresh water
Turn off the tap while you brush your teeth.
If everyone saves a little, together we can save a lot.

questions.q: How much of Earth's water is fresh water?
What should you do while brushing your teeth?
How can you reuse water?

keySentences.s: You can also reuse water.
Turn off the tap while you brush your teeth.

title: Birds That Cannot Fly
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. Instead, they are excellent swimmers. Their wings work like flippers and help them move quickly through the water to catch fish.
Most penguins live in the southern half of the world. Some live in very cold places like Antarctica, but others live on warmer coasts in South America and Africa.
Penguins often live in large groups. Parents take turns keeping their eggs warm and finding food. Today, some kinds of penguins are in danger because the oceans are changing.

penguin.def: a black and white bird that swims

wing.def: the part a bird uses to fly

coast.g: warmer coasts 較溫暖的海岸。

turn.def: the time for one person to do something

danger.g: be in danger 面臨危險。

grammar.ex: Instead, they are excellent swimmers.
Some live in very cold places like Antarctica, but others live on warmer coasts
Parents take turns keeping their eggs warm

questions.q: What are penguins very good at?
Where do most penguins live?
opts: In the southern half of the world

questions.q: Why are some penguins in danger?

keySentences.s: Penguins often live in large groups.
Instead, they are excellent swimmers.

title: The Story of Paper
note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Paper is so common that we rarely think about it. But for most of history, people wrote on stone, wood, cloth or animal skins.

Paper making was developed in ancient China about two thousand years ago. People mixed plant fibers with water, spread the mix thin and let it dry. Later, the idea slowly spread to other parts of the world.
Today, paper is made mostly from wood. Recycling paper saves trees, water and energy. Next time you finish with a newspaper or a box, put it in the recycling bin.

common.g: so common that… 如此常見以至於…。

rarely.g: 頻率副詞，本身就是否定意味。

history.g: for most of history 在歷史上大部分時間。

spread.def: to open out over a surface; to move to more places

grammar.ex: Paper is so common that we rarely think about it.
Paper making was developed in ancient China
spread the mix thin and let it dry

questions.q: What did people write on before paper?
Where was paper making developed?
What does recycling paper save?

keySentences.s: Today, paper is made mostly from wood.
Paper is so common that we rarely think about it.

title: The secret to a happy life: lessons from 8 decades of research
zh: 幸福人生的秘密：八十年研究的啟示

source.name: TED：Robert Waldinger, The secret to a happy life: lessons from 8 decades of research

note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: Robert Waldinger leads a famous study that has followed people's lives for more than eight decades. In this later talk, he shares more of what the study has taught him.
The main message is simple but powerful: our relationships matter a lot for a happy and healthy life. Good relationships are like muscles. If we do not use them, they get weaker.
He suggests small actions to keep relationships strong, like sending a message to an old friend or having a real conversation with someone at work. Who could you contact this week?

lead.g: leads 第三人稱單數；leader 名詞。

follow.def: to watch or go after something over time

matter.g: matter a lot 非常重要。

contact.def: to call or write to someone

grammar.ex: a famous study that has followed people's lives for more than eight decades
If we do not use them, they get weaker.
like sending a message to an old friend

questions.q: How long has the study followed people?
What are good relationships compared to?
Which small action does he suggest?
opts: Send a message to an old friend

keySentences.s: Who could you contact this week?
If we do not use them, they get weaker.
